title: The broker-dealer and the people inside it

reading.h: Broker vs dealer — agent vs principal
reading.body:
A single firm wears two hats, one trade at a time.

As a **broker (agent)** the firm *matches* a customer with someone else and charges a **commission**, disclosed separately on the confirmation. It never owns the security.

As a **dealer (principal)** the firm trades from *its own inventory* and is paid through a **markup** (on a sale to the customer) or **markdown** (on a purchase from the customer), built into the price.

The rule that gets tested: **a firm may not act as both broker and dealer on the same trade** — it cannot charge a commission and a markup on one transaction. The FINRA **5% policy** (Rule 2121) is a fairness *guideline* for markups and commissions, not a hard limit.

A **registered representative (RR)** is anyone who solicits or takes securities orders. To be one you must pass the **SIE plus a rep-level exam** (the Series 7 is the General Securities Representative license), be **fingerprinted**, be **sponsored by a member firm**, and have **Form U4** filed for you. Disclosures on the U4 must be updated within **30 days**; on termination the firm files **Form U5** within 30 days.

**Statutory disqualification** can bar someone — for example, a felony or a securities-related misdemeanor within the past 10 years. Continuing education has two parts: the **Regulatory Element** (annually) and the **Firm Element** (annually).

A **principal** is a licensed **supervisor** (Series 24 general principal; Series 9/10 for sales/options supervision; Series 53 for municipals). A principal approves new accounts, discretionary trades, and communications, and handles complaints, under FINRA Rule 3110 (supervision).

A **market maker** is a *dealer* that continuously quotes a firm two-sided market — a bid and an ask — in a security and stands ready to trade at those prices, profiting on the spread.

A **Designated Market Maker (DMM)** is the NYSE's version, with affirmative and negative obligations to keep a fair and orderly market. Distinguish the roles: the RR sells, the principal supervises, the market maker/DMM provides liquidity.

Most retail firms split the work. An **introducing broker** holds the *customer relationship* — it takes the order and knows the client — but sends the trade to a **clearing (carrying) firm** that holds the assets, settles the trade, and sends statements. This is a *fully disclosed* arrangement when the clearing firm knows each customer.

A **prime broker** is a clearing/custody hub for hedge funds and other big clients that execute through many different *executing brokers* but keep everything in one place. Related institutional plumbing: **DVP/RVP** (delivery-versus-payment / receive-versus-payment) settlement, used when a customer's assets sit at a custodian bank.

Four acronyms recur, so keep them straight:

**DTCC** — the umbrella clearing-and-depository organization for stocks and bonds.
**NSCC** — a DTCC subsidiary that *clears* and nets equity trades between firms.
**DTC** — the *depository* that holds securities in street name (book-entry).
**OCC** — the Options Clearing Corporation, the *issuer and guarantor* of every listed option.

Supporting record-keepers: the **transfer agent** keeps shareholder records and issues/cancels certificates, the **registrar** audits the transfer agent to prevent over-issuance, and the **custodian** holds the assets. Do not confuse the transfer agent (keeps records) with the registrar (audits those records).

**Unregistered staff may not solicit orders, take orders, or receive transaction-based (commission) compensation** (FINRA 2040). They may do clerical work and hand out material with no discussion. Crossing that line — an assistant 'just placing' a customer's order — is a violation.

reading.h: The conduct rules at headline level
reading.body:
The organization chart comes with a conduct rulebook. Know each at headline level:

**Gifts (FINRA 3220):** capped per person per year — the limit was raised to **$300** effective 2026-03-30 (from the long-standing $100). Business entertainment where the rep attends is separate.
**Outside business activity (3270):** prior *written notice* to the firm.
**Private securities transactions / 'selling away' (3280):** written notice, plus firm *approval* if the rep is compensated.
**Political contributions (MSRB G-37):** a $250 de minimis per election to a candidate you can vote for; exceeding it triggers a 2-year ban on negotiated muni business.
**Borrowing from / lending to customers (3240):** generally prohibited.
**Sharing in a customer account (2150):** only with written approval and pro rata to the rep's own contribution.
**Guaranteeing a customer against loss:** prohibited.

flashcards.front: Agent vs principal — how is each paid?
flashcards.back: Agent (broker) matches buyer and seller, earns a commission. Principal (dealer) trades from inventory, earns a markup/markdown built into the price.

flashcards.front: Can a firm charge a commission AND a markup on one trade?
flashcards.back: No — a firm may act in only one capacity (agent OR principal) per trade.
A fairness GUIDELINE (Rule 2121) for markups/commissions/markdowns — not a hard 5% limit.
U4 = registration application (filed by the firm; updates within 30 days). U5 = termination filing (within 30 days).
Series 24 = general principal; Series 9/10 = sales/options supervision; Series 53 = municipal principal. Principals supervise under Rule 3110.
DTCC = clearing/depository umbrella; NSCC = clears/nets equity trades; DTC = depository (street name); OCC = issuer & guarantor of listed options.
Transfer agent keeps shareholder records and issues/cancels certificates; registrar audits the transfer agent to prevent over-issuance.
Introducing broker holds the customer relationship/takes the order; clearing (carrying) firm holds assets, settles, and sends statements.

flashcards.front: What may an UNREGISTERED person NOT do?
flashcards.back: Solicit orders, take orders, or receive commission (transaction-based) pay. Clerical work only (FINRA 2040).
Outside business activity = prior written notice. Private securities transaction = written notice + firm approval if compensated.

flashcards.front: Gift limit and political-contribution de minimis
flashcards.back: Gifts capped at $300/person/year (FINRA 3220, raised 2026-03-30). MSRB G-37: $250 per election to a candidate you can vote for; over that = 2-year ban.
A clearing/custody hub for a hedge fund that executes through many executing brokers but keeps assets in one place.

quiz.stem: A broker-dealer fills a customer's buy order by selling shares out of its own inventory. In this trade the firm is compensated by:
options: A markup built into the price the customer pays
A commission disclosed separately on the confirmation
A commission plus a markup on the same trade
A management fee based on the customer's assets
quiz.explanation: Selling from inventory is acting as a dealer (principal), which is compensated by a markup. A commission is the broker (agent) capacity, and a firm may not charge both on a single trade.

quiz.stem: A firm takes a customer's order and routes it to another party to find the other side of the trade, without ever owning the security. In this transaction the firm is acting as a(n):
options: Dealer, earning a markup
Principal, earning a markdown
Agent, earning a commission
Market maker, earning the spread
quiz.explanation: Matching a customer with a third party without holding the security is the agent (broker) capacity, compensated by a commission. Acting as a dealer/principal or market maker would mean trading from the firm's own inventory.

quiz.stem: Which organization is the issuer and guarantor of every listed option?
options: The DTC
The NSCC
The OCC
The transfer agent
quiz.explanation: The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) issues and guarantees every listed option. The DTC is the depository for stocks/bonds, the NSCC clears equity trades, and the transfer agent keeps shareholder records — none of which guarantee options.

quiz.stem: In a fully disclosed clearing arrangement, which firm holds the customer's assets, settles trades, and mails account statements?
options: The introducing broker
The clearing (carrying) firm
The prime broker's executing broker
The transfer agent
quiz.explanation: The clearing (carrying) firm holds assets, settles, and sends statements; the introducing broker holds the customer relationship and takes the order but does not carry the account. The transfer agent handles issuer share records, not customer accounts.

quiz.stem: An unregistered sales assistant at a broker-dealer may do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Perform clerical and administrative tasks
Distribute approved marketing material without discussing it
Accept and enter a customer's securities order
Schedule appointments for a registered representative
quiz.explanation: An unregistered person may not solicit or accept securities orders or receive transaction-based pay (FINRA 2040). Clerical work, handing out approved material without discussion, and scheduling are permitted.

quiz.stem: Which pair correctly distinguishes the transfer agent from the registrar?
options: The transfer agent audits share counts; the registrar issues certificates
The transfer agent keeps shareholder records and issues/cancels certificates; the registrar audits the transfer agent to prevent over-issuance
Both perform the same function for different exchanges
The registrar holds the securities in street name; the transfer agent clears trades
quiz.explanation: The transfer agent keeps shareholder records and issues/cancels certificates; the registrar audits the transfer agent to ensure the number of shares outstanding is not exceeded. Holding securities in street name is the DTC's role, not the registrar's.

quiz.stem: A registered representative wants to sell an investment away from the firm and will be compensated for it. Under the private securities transaction rule (FINRA 3280), the representative must:
options: Do nothing, because compensated outside transactions are exempt
Provide only oral notice to a supervisor
Provide prior written notice AND obtain the firm's approval
Provide written notice only, with no approval required
quiz.explanation: For a compensated private securities transaction (selling away), Rule 3280 requires prior written notice AND the firm's approval; the firm then supervises it as its own. Written notice alone (no approval) is the standard for an uncompensated OBA under Rule 3270, not a compensated PST.
